title_ar: تقريظ  الشيخ الددو لكتاب إرشاد المهرة  في أسانيد المحضرة للشيخ العلامة محمد يحظيه بن محمد عالي
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew’s Commendation of the Book Irshad al-Maharah fi Asanid al-Mahdarah by the Learned Shaykh Muhammad Yahzih ibn Muhammad Ali
body_ar: تقريظ الشيخ الددو لكتاب إرشاد المهرة في أسانيد المحضرة للشيخ العلامة محمد يحظيه بن محمد عالي تقريظ فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو لكتاب إرشاد المهرة في أسانيد المحضرة لفضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد يحظيه بن محمد عالي بن محمد فال بن نعم العبد المجلسي كتاب جليل جل في عالم الكتب و جدد في التاريخ في المنكب الغربي و سد فراغا كان في مكتباتنا بوصل أسانيد المحاضر و الكتب و أنشر ما قد كان طول المدى طوى و أقبر من آثار آسادها الغلب و أرشد أصحاب المهارة و الهدى لأنفع طرق السير في أثر الركب و أبدى به الشيخ الإمام عجائبا بها عجب يهدي و يشفي من العجب محمد يحظيه الكريم سراجنا مجلي سباق العلم في السبسب السهب محط رحال الدارسين مجرب لوضع الهناء في مواضع ذي النقب بحيث يقاني العلم و الفهم و التقى مع الجود و الأخلاق جنبا إلى جنب مع الأدب الراقي و شعر مهذب و ذوق رفيع لا يحيد عن الدرب إلى نسب في العز و المجد باذخ ترقى من الأعياص في المرتقى الصعب أبو أحمد الندب الكريم أبوهمُ تناقل عنه المجد ندب إلى ندب و قد خلقت للفهم ظرفا صدورهم و أعمارهم للشغل بالفرض و الندب و أرجلهم للسبق في سبل العلى و أيديهمُ للبذل و البحث و الكتب لقد بلغوا في المجد و العز و العلى مراتب قصوى لا تقرب بالنجب و في مجلس العلم المهيب توسطوا بصدر به كانوا بمنزلة القلب لدى قبة الإسلام معقل عزهم على الطائر الميمون و المنزل الرحب كما آل نعم العبد للناس نعمة موطأة الأكناف كالمنهل العذب مطاعين في الهيجا مصابيح في الدجى مفاتيح أغلاق مفاريج للكرب و ذا الشيخ يقفو من أبيه شمائلا يساويه في كل المفاخر أو يربي تآليفه ضن الزمان بمثلها لها السبق مضمون على البعد و القرب كأن أبا حيان يقصد كتبه بأبياته إذ قال في البحر و الضرب مشارق أنوار تبدت بسبتة فواعجبا تبدو المشارق بالغرب و مرعى خصيب في جديب ربوعها ألا فاعجبوا للخصب في موضع الجدب فما فضل الأرجاء إلا رجالها و إلا فلا فضل لترب على ترب
body_en:
Sheikh al-Dedew's commendation of the book *Irshad al-Maharah fi Asanid al-Mahdarah* by the learned Shaykh Muhammad Yahzih ibn Muhammad Ali.

The commendation of the eminent Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew of the book *Irshad al-Maharah fi Asanid al-Mahdarah*, by the eminent and learned Shaykh Muhammad Yahzih ibn Muhammad Ali ibn Muhammad Fal ibn Naam al-Abd al-Majlisi.

[Verse. Rendered as prose, line by line; the Arabic is the operative text.]

*A noble book, exalted in the world of books, which broke new ground in the history of the Western Flank,*

*and closed a gap that stood in our libraries, by joining up the chains of transmission (asānīd) of the traditional schools and of the books,*

*and spread out again what the long passage of time had folded away and buried of the traces of its conquering lions,*

*and guided the skilled and the rightly directed to the most profitable ways of travelling in the track of the caravan.*

*By it the Shaykh, the Imam, brought to light wonders at which one marvels — wonders that guide, and that cure a man of marvelling.*

*Muhammad Yahzih, the noble, is our lamp, first past the post in the race of knowledge across the wide and open waste,*

*the halting-place where students unload their mounts, one practised at laying the tar-salve exactly where the mange is,*

*such that in him knowledge, understanding and God-consciousness (taqwā) stand side by side with generosity and good character,*

*together with an elevated literary art, finely turned verse, and a refined taste that never strays from the road —*

*all of it joined to a lineage of towering honour and glory, risen from noble stock by the steep ascent.*

*Abu Ahmad, the noble and ready man, was their father; glory has been passed down from him, ready man to ready man.*

*Their breasts were created as vessels for understanding, and their lifetimes for occupation with the obligatory (farḍ) and the recommended (nadb);*

*their feet for outstripping others on the paths of eminence, and their hands for giving, for enquiry and for writing.*

*In glory, honour and eminence they have reached the furthest ranks, not to be approached even by the noblest of men;*

*and in the awe-inspiring assembly of learning they took the middle place, at a forefront where they stood as the heart stands.*

*At the Dome of Islam is the stronghold of their honour, under a lucky star and in a spacious dwelling.*

*So too the house of Naam al-Abd have been a blessing to people, level-spread in their hospitality, like a sweet watering place:*

*obeyed in the thick of battle, lamps in the darkness, keys to what is locked, deliverers from distress.*

*And this Shaykh follows his father in his qualities, matching him in every title to glory, or surpassing him.*

*Time has begrudged the world the like of his writings; their precedence is assured, far and near.*

*It is as though Abu Hayyan meant his books by the lines he spoke in al-Bahr wa-l-Darb:*

*"Easterly risings of lights that shone forth at Ceuta — and what a wonder, that the risings should appear in the West!"*

*A fertile pasture amid the barrenness of its lands — marvel, then, at fertility in the place of drought!*

*For regions have no merit except through their men; failing that, no soil has any merit over soil.*

flags.arabic: و أعمارهم للشغل بالفرض و الندب
flags.context: و قد خلقت للفهم ظرفا صدورهم و أعمارهم للشغل بالفرض و الندب, two lines after أبو أحمد الندب الكريم أبوهم ... ندب إلى ندب
options: "occupation with the obligatory (farḍ) and the recommended (nadb)" — the two legal categories of act
"occupation with what is required of them and what is asked of them", non-technical
"occupation with religious duty and with generous deeds", reading ندب against the earlier sense
flags.note: Here فرض and ندب ARE the legal categories and the fixed five-rulings mapping applies (style guide section 3): obligatory and recommended. The reason for flagging is the pun — two lines earlier ندب is used twice in its other sense, "a ready, capable man" (الندب الكريم ... ندب إلى ندب), which English cannot carry across both places. A reviewer should decide whether to footnote the wordplay.

flags.arabic: كأن أبا حيان يقصد كتبه بأبياته إذ قال في البحر و الضرب ... مشارق أنوار تبدت بسبتة
flags.context: the closing movement of the ode
options: the source attributes to Abu Hayyan lines that are commonly cited in praise of al-Qadi Iyad’s Mashāriq al-Anwār, a work written at Ceuta — a possible misattribution in the source
Abu Hayyan al-Gharnati is indeed quoting or reworking those lines, and the ascription is correct
في البحر و الضرب names a work or a metre and the phrase has been garbled in transmission
flags.note: Two separate uncertainties in one couplet. First, the celebrated lines مشارق أنوار تبدت بسبتة are conventionally cited of al-Qadi Iyad’s Mashāriq al-Anwār, composed at Ceuta, not of Abu Hayyan’s own work; the ascription here may be an error in the source. Second, في البحر و الضرب is opaque — البحر suggests Abu Hayyan’s tafsīr al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ, but الضرب does not answer to a known title. Translated exactly as it stands and flagged; not corrected from memory (style guide section 11).

flags.arabic: بحيث يقاني العلم و الفهم و التقى
flags.context: in praise of the book’s author
options: "such that in him knowledge, understanding and God-consciousness stand matched side by side"
reading يقاني as يقارن, "he sets alongside / combines"
the word is corrupt in the source and the intended verb cannot be recovered
flags.note: يقاني is not a standard form in this construction. The sense demanded by جنبا إلى جنب at the end of the line is one of combining or matching, which options 0 and 1 both give. Left unresolved rather than emended.

options: "at the Dome of Islam", a title borne by more than one city and here most likely a specific Mauritanian or regional centre
a figurative expression for the heart of the Muslim world, with no particular place intended
a proper place name that should be transliterated rather than translated
flags.note: قبة الإسلام is historically applied to several cities. The record gives no context to fix the referent. Rendered literally with capitals so that a reviewer can substitute a place name if the Sheikh’s office identifies one.

translator_notes: A commendatory ode (taqrīẓ) in verse, preceded by a prose ascription, not a fatwa. type is set to "article" for want of a verse type in the schema; the text states no legal ruling.
Rendered as prose line by line per style guide section 4; no rhymed English attempted, and the Arabic is retained as the operative text.

The body as served opens by repeating the article title verbatim before the fuller prose ascription. This is CMS furniture inside the body rather than authorial text, but it has been preserved in body_ar and carried into body_en rather than silently dropped (style guide section 11).

المنكب الغربي, "the Western Flank", is the classical designation of the far Maghrib and specifically of the Mauritanian region. Kept literal, since the geographic self-description is part of the poem’s point.

المحضرة / المحاضر: the Mauritanian traditional school (maḥẓarah) is spelled throughout with ḍād rather than ẓāʾ, both in the book title and in the plural. Preserved as found and not corrected; the term is not yet in the glossary.
لوضع الهناء في مواضع ذي النقب draws on the proverb يضع الهناء مواضع النقب — applying the tar-salve exactly where the mange is — an image of precision. Translated literally so the image survives.
